topic: Finding a Needle in a Digital Haystack: Understanding Grover's Algorithm
target_audience: Undergraduate students with basic linear algebra knowledge and an interest in quantum computing

sections.title: The Search Dilemma: Classical vs. Quantum
lecture_lines: Imagine searching for one item in N unsorted boxes.
Classically, searching takes N/2 attempts on average.
Grover's quantum algorithm takes only square root of N.
animations: Title fade in.
Grid search highlight.
Target found highlight.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Superposition Wavefront
lecture_lines: We begin by putting qubits into equal superposition.
The Hadamard transform distributes probability across all boxes.
Every potential answer now has an identical amplitude.
animations: Show four horizontal ket labels: |00>, |01>, |10>, |11> in #FFFFFF.
Four square boxes containing the letter 'H' (#00FFCC) fade in above the labels.
A white horizontal baseline (#FFFFFF) appears; labels are moved below it.
Four bars grow from the baseline to an equal height of 2 units. Color: #00FFCC.
Text 'Equal Superposition' and 'alpha = 1/sqrt(N)' appear in #FFFFFF above the bars.

sections.title: Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
lecture_lines: An Oracle identifies the target state among all boxes.
It flips the target's sign, making its amplitude negative.
Visually, the target bar points downwards below the axis.
All other incorrect bars remain positive and unchanged.
This phase inversion marks the item we seek.
animations: Start with four equal cyan (#00FFCC) bars. The |11> label below the fourth bar turns gold #FFD700.
A red-orange box labeled 'Oracle' (#FF5555) fades in and hovers above the |11> bar.
The |11> bar pulses with gold light (#FFD700) to indicate identification.
The |11> bar reflects vertically across the baseline to a height of -2 units. Color changes to #FF5555.
The Oracle box fades out, and text 'Phase Inversion' (#FF5555) appears.

sections.title: Step 2: Amplitude Amplification (Inversion about the Mean)
lecture_lines: Next, we apply the Grover diffusion operator.
We calculate the average height of all bars.
Each bar is reflected across this average line.
The negative target bar now shoots significantly higher.
This process is known as amplitude amplification.
animations: Display the three positive bars (#00FFCC) and one negative bar (#FF5555).
A white dashed horizontal line (#FFFFFF) appears at height 1.0. Label 'Mean' (#FFFFFF) is added.
Four white vertical arrows (#FFFFFF) appear, showing the distance from each bar's top to the dashed line.
All bars reflect across the dashed line: |11> becomes height +4, others drop to 0.
The tall |11> bar turns gold (#FFD700). Label 'Amplitude Amplification' (#00FFCC) appears.

sections.title: The Harvest: Measurement and Speedup
lecture_lines: Repeating these steps maximizes the target's probability.
Final measurement yields the correct answer with near certainty.
This provides a quadratic speedup over classical searching.
animations: Show the tall gold bar (#FFD700) and three empty state slots. A circular arrow icon (#FFFFFF) indicates repetition.
A white arrow points at the tall bar as it flashes white. Text 'Measurement' (#FFFFFF) appears.
The text 'Success probability approx 100%!' and 'Grover's Speedup' appear in #00FFCC as the screen fades.
